old: Folic acid doses: prevention of neural tube defects = 400 mcg (0.4 mg) daily (start before conception and continue for first 12 weeks). Treatment of folate deficiency = 5 mg daily. Higher dose (5 mg daily before conception and for first 12 weeks) is recommended for women at high risk of NTDs (prior NTD, diabetes, obesity, antiepileptics).
new: Folic acid doses: prevention of neural tube defects = 400 mcg (0.4 mg) daily (start before conception and continue for first 12 weeks). Treatment of folate deficiency = 5 mg daily. Higher dose (5 mg daily before conception and for first 12 weeks) is offered to women at increased risk of NTDs (NICE NG247: personal, partner or family history of NTD, previous affected pregnancy, type 1 or type 2 diabetes, sickle cell disease or thalassaemia, antiepileptic or HIV medicines). A raised BMI alone does not need more than 400 mcg.

old: CURB-65: Confusion, Urea >7, RR ≥30, systolic BP <90 or diastolic ≤60 mmHg, age ≥65. Score 0-1 = home, 2 = consider admission, ≥3 = admit.
new: CURB65: Confusion, Urea >7 mmol/L, RR ≥30, systolic BP <90 or diastolic ≤60 mmHg, age ≥65. NICE NG250: 0–1 = consider discharge home with primary care follow-up and safety-netting; 2 = consider a virtual ward, SDEC unit, hospital at home or inpatient care; ≥3 = consider inpatient care, with critical care referral if appropriate.

old: CURB-65 ≥3: admit and treat with IV antibiotics.
new: CURB65 ≥3: admit; give IV antibiotics when the person cannot take oral medicines or severity requires it (as here), and review IV treatment by 48 hours (NICE NG250).

old: B. Corticosteroids are not routine treatment for community-acquired pneumonia. C. Antibiotics should not be delayed awaiting culture results. D. Focal consolidation with productive cough suggests bacterial pneumonia; antivirals are not routine. E. Insulin treats hyperglycaemia.
new: B. Corticosteroids are not routine treatment for community-acquired pneumonia; NICE NG250 advises considering them (starting with IV hydrocortisone), in addition to antibiotics, only for adults with high-severity pneumonia in hospital. C. Antibiotics should not be delayed awaiting culture results. D. Focal consolidation with productive cough suggests bacterial pneumonia; antivirals are not routine. E. Insulin treats hyperglycaemia.
